significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that across a large class of jailbreaks, harm remains decodable at earlier prompt positions while its projection into the final decision position collapses, and that restoring this routing restores refusal; this is both a behavioral phenomenon and a causal mechanism, with a form-(iii) predictive coupling between the position-wise "aggregation gap" and jailbreak success. That conclusion would constrain how future jailbreak failures are explained—representation erasure versus read-out failure—and would materially qualify the refusal mechanism characterized in Arditi et al., "Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction" (NeurIPS 2024), rather than merely identify another safety direction. The claim is determinate, and a negative result in which attacks also erase the earlier-position signal would rule out the proposed aggregation account and its representation/read-out taxonomy, so both branches are informative. In the topic-substitution check, replacing this positional routing hypothesis with generic mechanistic LLM safety would not justify this score; the above-median value comes specifically from the asserted cross-attack coupling and causal decomposition.

reach.justification: The concrete handle is the "distributed-aggregation monitor" that pools "the harm signal across all prompt positions," an ex-ante input diagnostic that can flag a harmful request before generation and thus gives auditors or deployment systems an action window. After per-model re-extraction, the conclusion predicts more than where to look: it predicts preserved harm projections at harm-bearing positions, a collapsed final-position projection, and improved detection from position-wise aggregation, so a measurable relation survives recalibration. The hypothesis asserts applicability to "a large class of jailbreaks" and safety-aligned LLMs generally, while acknowledging attacks that erase harm at all positions; its immediate downstream users could therefore include guardrail builders and model deployers, not only mechanistic-interpretability researchers. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: generic interpretability-based safety supplies neither this named monitor nor its ex-ante positional read-out rule.
